question.explanation: The sum takes integer values of $n$ from $1$ to $4.$ So, computing the terms for $n=1,2,3,4$ and then adding them, we get \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \sum\limits_{n = 1}^4 \dfrac{3n + 2} 6 &= \left( {{\dfrac { 3\left( 1 \right) + 2} 6}} \right) + \left( {{\dfrac {3\left( 2 \right) + 2} 6}} \right) + \left( {{\dfrac {3\left( 3 \right) + 2} 6}} \right) + \left( {{\dfrac {3\left( 4 \right) + 2} 6}} \right) \\[0pt] &= \left( {{\dfrac {3 + 2} 6}} \right) + \left( {{\dfrac {6 + 2} 6}} \right) + \left( {{\dfrac {9 + 2} 6}} \right) + \left( {{\dfrac {12 + 2} 6}} \right) \\[5pt] &= {\dfrac 5 6} + {\dfrac8 6} + {\dfrac{11} 6} + {\dfrac{14} 6} \\[5pt] &= {\dfrac{5 + 8 + 11 + 14} 6} \\[5pt] &= {\dfrac{38} 6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\cancel{2}\cdot 19} {\cancel{2}\cdot 3} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{19}{3}. \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating Expressions Written in Sigma Notation

question.explanation:
Notice that the terms of the corresponding sequence

\[ 5, \quad 10, \quad 15, \quad \ldots, \quad 145, \quad 150. \] are multiples of $5,$ and since $150\div 5= 30,$ there are $30$ terms in total.

Therefore, the $n$th term of the sequence has the form \[ a_n =5n, \] where $n$ ranges from $n=1$ to $n=30.$ Indeed:

\begin{align*} a_1 &= 5(1) =5 \\[5pt] a_2 &=5(2) =10 \\[5pt] a_3 &=5(3) =15 \\[3pt] & \:\:\vdots \\[3pt] a_{29} &= 5(29) = 145 \\[5pt] a_{30} &= 5(30) =150 \end{align*}

Therefore,

\[ \eqalign{ S=5+10+15+\cdots+145+150=\sum_{n=1}^{30} 5n. } \]

The sum takes integer values of $a$ from $1$ to $3.$ So, computing the terms for $a=1,2,3$ and then adding them, we get \begin{align*} \displaystyle\sum_{a=1}^3a\left(\dfrac12\right)^{a+1} &=1\left(\dfrac12\right)^{1+1}+2\left(\dfrac12\right)^{2+1} +3\left(\dfrac12\right)^{3+1}\\[0pt] &=1\left(\dfrac12\right)^{2}+2\left(\dfrac12\right)^{3}+3\left(\dfrac12\right)^{4}\\[5pt] &=1\cdot \dfrac14 +2\cdot\dfrac{1}{8}+3\cdot \dfrac1{16}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac1{4}+\dfrac2{8}+\dfrac3{16}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{(1\cdot 4) + (2\cdot 2 ) +3}{16}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4+4+3}{16}\\[5pt] &=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{11}{16}}. \end{align*}

example.title: Evaluating Expressions Written in Sigma Notation

question.explanation:
Notice that the terms of the corresponding sequence \[ 11, \quad 22, \quad 33, \quad \ldots, \quad 242, \quad 253. \] are multiples of $11.$ Since $253\div 11 = 23,$ there are $23$ terms in total.

Therefore, the $n$th term of the sequence has the form \[ a_n =11n, \] where $n$ ranges from $n=1$ to $n=23.$ Indeed:

\begin{align*} a_1 &= 11(1) = 11 \\[5pt] a_2 &=11(2) = 22 \\[5pt] a_3 &=11(3) = 33 \\ & \:\:\vdots \\[3pt] a_{22} &= 11(22) = 242 \\[5pt] a_{23} &= 11(23) = 253 \end{align*}

Therefore, \[ S= 11+22+33+\cdots +242+253 = \sum_{n=1}^{\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{23}}\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 11n}. \]
